metadata.note: CLI explainer (cli-explainer skill — ADVANCED tier), built on D:\ai1-cli-main per CLAUDE.md rule 3. Folder dated 2026-09-08 per explicit instruction. Follows the mandatory CLI spine: INTRO → PROBLEM → CLI/CODE/OUTPUT → revision cycle CLI/CODE/OUTPUT → SUMMARY → NEXT STEPS → OUTRO; THE REVISION LAW satisfied by one full revision cycle. ACTUAL-CODE LAW: code/ holds four REAL runnable scripts (corpus.py, encoder.py, bm25_search.py, hybrid_search.py); both CODE beats quote them verbatim and every number in every OUTPUT beat is captured stdout, saved as _run-bm25.txt and _run-hybrid.txt. Dense retrieval uses REAL all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from the local HuggingFace cache — encoder.py parses safetensors and runs the 6-layer BERT forward pass in numpy because sentence-transformers is not installed here; validated behaviourally (identical 1.000 / paraphrase 0.555 / unrelated 0.100). Nothing is hand-tuned. THE FINDING IS NOT THE TIDY ONE and the reel says so: dense won BOTH queries, and the fused hybrid LOST the paraphrase by 0.00025 — which independently reproduces the chapter's own refusal to claim hybrid always wins. B04 reuses CliRunOutput and B09 reuses RagExecutiveSummary, props-only. B01/B07/B08 are three new bespoke components (RetrievalTwoQueries, RetrievalMatrix, RrfMargin) — GATE L searched four ways and every close lead (BrandDriftCaseStudy, CwcEvalScoring, CadencesFig3Artifacts) exposes only sparkLine/activeColumn, i.e. content hardcoded to another reel. props.caption: Chapter 6's worked example: one gold passage, two queries with almost nothing in common.

beats.narration_text: The ask: sparse retrieval, from scratch. B-M-twenty-five — term frequency, inverse document frequency, length normalisation, and saturation, so a word repeated fifty times doesn't count fifty times. One detail matters more than it looks: tokenise so T-R-one-fourteen survives as a single term. Split it into t-r and one-fourteen, and the exact-match signal is gone before we start.

Send arms; runningText 'generating script…'

props.command: claude "write bm25_search.py — BM25 from scratch over 12 help-desk policy passages, with IDF, length normalisation and term-frequency saturation. Tokenise so TR-114 stays ONE term. Run both queries and report whether top-1 is the gold passage."

beats.narration_text: Read the scoring function. Every query term contributes its inverse document frequency, scaled by how often it appears in this passage — and that contribution saturates, so repetition stops paying. The normaliser divides by document length, so a long passage can't win just by being long. And T-R-one-fourteen appears in exactly one of twelve passages, which gives it the highest I-D-F in the collection.

show.event: Code card lands, filename in the title bar
the TOKEN regex — hyphens kept inside a term, so TR-114 survives
idf() — rare terms score far higher than common ones
spark line settles: rare words carry the weight

props.title: bm25_search.py — Claude Code output

beats.narration_text: Run it. The code query: T-R-one-fourteen wins at three point four nine, ahead of two other policies that also contain the word reimbursement. Sparse nails it. Now the paraphrase: help pay for grad school returns the certification-exam policy, at three point eight two, because that passage literally contains the words company pays. The right answer is third. That is the paraphrase gap, measured.

beats.role_note: SHORT CUT: narration and props rewritten. The 16:9 summary reported dense and hybrid results; this cut drops the revision cycle per THE REVISION LAW's 9:16 exception, so it would describe outcomes the viewer never sees.
beats.narration_text: So: BM25 does exactly what it promises. It matched a rare code that nothing else in the collection contained, and it ranked the right passage third when the question shared almost no words with it. That is not a bug in the implementation — it is what matching on literal terms means. The fix is a second retriever that matches on meaning instead.

Subline resolves: the two failure modes are complementary, the fusion is not free

props.headline: The blind spot IS the design.
props.subline: BM25 found a rare code nothing else contained, and missed a question that shared almost no words with its answer. Matching literal terms is the strength and the limit, in the same mechanism.

beats.role_note: SHORT CUT: handoff rewritten. The 16:9 prompt asks the viewer to build all three retrievers and show 'the rank arithmetic that made it lose' — arithmetic shown in B08, which this cut drops. The replacement follows from what the short DOES show: sparse wins some queries and loses others; find out what the losses share.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: 'Take twenty real questions people ask about my documents, run them through a keyword search, and split them into the ones it answers and the ones it misses. Then tell me what the misses have in common.' That last sentence is the one worth having. Any search will hand you a hit rate; asking what the failures share is what tells you whether you need a second retriever at all — and what it would have to be good at.
